chunks: It is not that simple.

Explain why a proposed solution overlooks a complication.
It/That + is not that simple; follow with the overlooked reason.
That expresses degree. Source rejects choosing sides too easily; everyday examples transfer the same function without borrowing case allegations.
家人建议直接搬到便宜的公寓，但你还要考虑通勤时间。

at least in my personal experience
至少就我的个人经验而言
Limit a general statement to your own experience.
Place the phrase before or after a claim; it limits evidence, not numerical quantity.
The insurance claim is explicitly personal experience. New examples do not present broad claims as established facts.

Just something to keep in mind
有一点供你参考／提醒你留意
Offer a relevant caution without issuing a direct command.
State a fact, then add just something to keep in mind; keep in mind means remember when deciding.
Fragment works as a conversational aside. Complete teaching examples provide the actual caution missing from generic prompts.
家人准备周日晚去买东西，你提醒他附近商店那天会提早关门。

They don't like to ...
他们不愿意／不喜欢……
Describe someone's usual reluctance or preference.
They/we/I don't like to + base verb; he/she doesn't like to + base verb.
A preference, not an inability or prohibition. Don't expands to do not; the verb after to stays in base form.

With that being said
话虽如此；说完这些
Move on after acknowledging the preceding point, sometimes adding a contrast.
With that being said, + a complete clause. It can signal transition as well as concession.
At segment 148 it resumes the main discussion rather than contradicting the disclaimer. Do not teach every occurrence as however.
